provenance.note: Written from the artifact repository (README, Svelte components, TypeScript sources) plus one 82-second recording and its DOM/attribute surveys. WizMap is a scalable interactive visualisation for exploring large machine-learning embeddings (Wang, Hohman and Chau, ACL'23 demo). The interface is one document: a zoomable embedding map drawn in WebGL canvases and SVG, a top control bar (Contour / Point / Grid / Label / Time), a left search panel, a bottom-right footer with zoom and embedding-chooser buttons, a draggable point-detail window and two tooltips. Its primary interactions are pan, zoom, wheel and hover, none of which the collector can record; almost everything below is therefore anchored either on the few clickable controls or on the text the map writes back onto the page when it redraws.

rules.note: This is the rule that recovers WizMap's main interaction, which the instrument cannot see. Wheel, drag and hover leave no events at all; what they do leave is a burst of new topic labels in g.topics. layoutTopicLabels() has six call sites: the first data load, zoomed(), zoomEnded(), the Number of Labels slider, the High Density Region checkbox and a group contour checkbox. The load is excluded by the index-0 rule above, and the three controls are excluded both by their own higher-priority rules and by the requirement that nothing was clicked, typed or pressed. There is no resize handler in the application, so a window resize does not redraw them either.
